transcript:
Meeting header: Date/time: 2026-09-29 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood Partnerships), Rita Kapoor (Helix Head of Partnerships), Tom Ellis (Helix VP Sales), Sandra Kim (Helix Solution Architect), Devon Reyes (Helix BDR)

Summary: quick pipeline review and co-sell strategy; align on pilot scope, sequencing, and next steps. Discussed potential accounts, technical constraints (latency/cost), and who owns outreach.

Topics: pipeline health, pilot bench-marking, pricing tiers, security questions, joint GTM cadence

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making the time, we'll try to keep this to 45 minutes. quick intros?
00:12 Rita Kapoor: Rita here - I run partnerships at Helix, we've got Tom and Sandra on the call - Tom runs GTM, Sandra is our solution architect.
00:20 Tom Ellis: hey all.
00:21 Sandra Kim: hi.
00:22 Maya Chen: awesome, so purpose of today is to walk through the co-sell pipeline we've been tracking, triage any blockers, and make sure we have clear owners for the pilot accounts. Liam will also cover a quick perf ask for the technical pilots.
00:35 Liam Ortiz: hi folks, yes i'll go over what we typically run for a pilot - small scaled load tests, a latency/cost matrix across model variants, and a quick check on VPC connectivity if you want private deployment. quick note: sometimes the transcript thinks VPC is VPC or vpc, so not important.
00:52 Devon Reyes: just to set context - Helix has five target accounts you mentioned in the sheet, two in finance, two in retail, one in healthcare, all pref mid-enterprise. We want to prioritize 2 for the Q4 outreach.
01:05 Maya Chen: cool, Rita — you flagged Account A and Account C as high-convert. Is that still correct?
01:12 Rita Kapoor: yes Account A (FinSolve) and Account C (RetailMax). FinSolve has stringent security needs - SOC2 plus on-prem logging and regional residency for EU customers.
01:25 Sandra Kim: on the tech side, FinSolve will require private deployment or at least VPC peering, and they care about encryption and KMS integration. RetailMax is more open to hosted but wants predictable latency under 300 ms p95.
01:40 Liam Ortiz: that aligns with what we've seen - hosted API can hit ~200-250 ms p95 for sequence lengths typical of RetailMax, but FinSolve's data rules push us towards Redwood Private or Dedicated. Also quantization can reduce latency/cost but may affect quality margin.
01:58 Tom Ellis: question on pricing — if we do a joint pilot and then convert, what's the typical deal split for co-sell? do you have standard templates?
02:06 Maya Chen: yes we have a partner playbook - Nina will own sharing the one-pager. usual co-sell is flexible; typical is referral/commission or reseller model depending on account. For larger deals we usually go to a joint demo and then AE to AE handoff.
02:18 Nina Park: i'll send the playbook after the call — it includes pricing bands, standard discounts for pilots, and case studies.
02:26 Rita Kapoor: perfect. on the pilot scoping — can Redwood support a 2-week perf test with ~500 concurrent reqs as a stress test?
02:36 Liam Ortiz: 500 concurrent is doable on Dedicated GPU pools; for hosted it depends on burst capacity. For the pilot we recommend Dedicated reserved for sustained load; we can spin up a short-term Dedicated cluster for the test. need to know model size (e.g., 13B vs 70B) and token lengths.
02:52 Sandra Kim: RetailMax use case is short customer message generation, avg 40 tokens. FinSolve is longer 150-200 tokens for summarization.
03:05 Liam Ortiz: okay short sequences are cheaper and faster, so RetailMax will do fine on a smaller backed model. For FinSolve, recommend a 13B with unquantized for fidelity initially, maybe try q4_0 quant later. we'll include latency/cost tradeoffs in the benchmark.
03:24 Tom Ellis: any red flags around compliance — we often get asked about audit logs and SSO.
03:30 Maya Chen: Redwood supports SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs; Private deployment can integrate with your customer's KMS/HSM for keys and retention policies. We also have SOC2 and ISO on the docs. we'll attach the security pack.
03:45 Rita Kapoor: great to know. can you also clarify data residency? FinSolve wants EU data to stay in EU.
03:50 Nina Park: yes we can region-lock and deploy to EU region or do on-prem for air-gapped. will share details in the security doc.
03:58 Devon Reyes: what's the expected timeline to get bench results? our outreach campaign starts mid-Oct.
04:03 Liam Ortiz: if we start next week we can have bench results in 5 business days, so by 2026-10-05. Need the sample prompts and token distribution today or tomorrow.
04:14 Rita Kapoor: we'll share prompts and sample payloads by 2026-10-01.
04:18 Maya Chen: good. next, pipeline review — Devon, can you run through the sheet?
04:22 Devon Reyes: sure, slide sheet notes - Account A (FinSolve) — likely conversion 60% stage: pilot, ARR estimate $220k, expected close Q1; Account B — smaller pilot $30k; Account C RetailMax — pilot interest high, ARR $180k; Account D/E earlier stage. total pipeline ~540k ARR across 5 accounts.
04:45 Maya Chen: ok that's promising. for co-sell motions, we recommend focusing on FinSolve and RetailMax as the joint pilot. We'll propose a play: Redwood handles inference runtime + security for the FinSolve pilot and Helix provides domain prompts and sales motion.
05:00 Tom Ellis: for outreach, who will own initial contact — Helix or Redwood?
05:04 Maya Chen: Helix can lead initial outreach since you have relationships, and we'll provide templated messaging and slides. then we do joint technical intro.
05:12 Devon Reyes: Devon will run the first outreach sequences.
05:15 Nina Park: Redwood marketing can support co-branded assets if you want — we have a co-sell template.
05:21 Rita Kapoor: yes please, that helps speed things up.
05:24 Tom Ellis: quick technical question — if we choose Dedicated for pilot, is there a minimum commit or contract?
05:29 Liam Ortiz: Dedicated typically has a minimum monthly commitment for reserved pools, but we can do short-term commitments or trial credits for pilots. For the pilot we can use a burstable pool and measure. We'll detail options in the pricing doc.
05:43 Sandra Kim: also want to ensure model version pinning — for audit we need reproducible outputs across runs.
05:49 Liam Ortiz: we support model pinning and rollbacks; KV cache and deterministic seeds are documented. minor transcript note: 'KV' sometimes transcribed as 'k v' so ignore.
06:02 Rita Kapoor: perfect. any competitive intel noticed? Helix said one prospect is also talking to Anthropic and an in-house build.
06:08 Maya Chen: ok we should note the strengths — Redwood's ops, predictable unit economics, and private deployment options is our angle.
06:15 Tom Ellis: can we get a short slide that compares Redwood to Anthropic/AWS Bedrock for procurement teams?
06:21 Nina Park: yes we'll produce a one-pager comparing feature sets and cost buckets; will call out private options and SLA differences.
06:30 Maya Chen: all right, recap of next steps — Liam will run benchmark and share by 2026-10-05, Maya/Nina will send co-sell one-pager and pricing by 2026-10-01, Rita will send prompts and account lists by 2026-10-01, Devon to start outreach sequence and share initial results week of 10/4, schedule intro between Tom and Redwood sales lead for 2026-10-06.
06:52 Rita Kapoor: sounds good. any final questions?
06:55 Tom Ellis: none from me.
06:56 Sandra Kim: no.
06:57 Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the attachments.
06:59 Meeting end

Action items (auto-summary):
- Maya to share co-sell one-pager, pricing bands, and partner playbook
- Liam to run performance and latency/cost benchmarks for pilot models
- Rita to share prompts, payloads, and target account list
- Devon to run initial outreach and share results

Attachments referenced: co-sell-playbook.pdf (shared), partner-pricing.xlsx (to be shared), pipeline-tracker (Google sheet link), security-pack.zip (Redwood SOC2/ISO and KMS details)

Notes on transcription: medium quality auto-transcript; occasional mishears (e.g., model names, acronyms) and dropped punctuation.

End of transcript.
